correctness.rationale: For the unnormalized Walsh coefficient on labelled edge sets, signed matrix-tree weights give exactly the signed tree sum. The deleted left vertex leaves an invertible right diagonal block with entries d in {±1,±3}, so the stated two-dimensional Schur test is equivalent to vanishing. Substituting all sign patterns gives the stated 3Q matrices: no negatives gives zero, singles give rank one with distinct kernels, doubles have determinant 180 and positive diagonals, and the triple has determinant 300 and positive diagonals. The base B is positive definite. Summing gives strict definiteness when 4|S|<n, and at equality singularity exactly when every nonzero local Q is a single of the same left type. The q right neighbors are distinct, q>=1 makes the three left choices disjoint, and characters diagonalize the specified counting convolution. The exact analytic proof covers every n>=2; the nested checks/verify_k3n.py was inspected as corroborative code, not executed or needed for the general theorem. The direct independent derivation from the earlier pointwise formula is given below.

evidence: The earlier v_i=(a_i b_i,a_i c_i,b_i c_i)/(a_i+b_i+c_i) equals (1/3,1/3,1/3) on a clean column. Every coordinate is at least -1 on any column. With m marked columns and k marked edges, every coordinate of the total is at least (n-4m)/3 >= (n-4k)/3.

For n=4k, strict positivity still holds if m<k. Otherwise each marked column is a single negative: adding (1,1,1) to its vector gives 2 times a coordinate vector, with the three coordinates in bijection with the left types. At equality the clean columns cancel the (-1,-1,-1) contribution from each marked column, leaving the sum of those nonnegative coordinate vectors.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For a strictly positive coordinate triple Phi>0; for a nonnegative one Phi=0 exactly when at most one coordinate is positive. Hence the earlier identity gives nonvanishing below degree n/4, and at equality requires all singleton columns of the same left type. That gives the exact three-center count and the convolution assertion follows by diagonalization. No new zero-solving theorem is required beyond this direct coordinate comparison.

value.rationale: The low-degree invertibility question is natural, but for this fixed graph family the proposed standalone contribution reduces to bounding each coordinate of an already known coefficient formula by its smallest possible single-column value and checking equality of the three singleton sign patterns. The counting and Fourier consequence are immediate once that is done. It supplies neither a new nontrivial invariant calculation beyond that direct deduction nor a broader rigidity mechanism or graph-family theorem.
